newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BANK PROCEDURES EASED FOR S.AFRICAN BROKERS.
newsitem.headline: BANK PROCEDURES EASED FOR S.AFRICAN BROKERS.

text.p: Two bills were amended by South Africa's parliamentary finance committee on Friday to make it easier for brokers to meet their legal obligation to keep clients' funds in trust accounts.

Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) legal counsel Nicky Newton-King told the committee that the changes would allow members of the JSE and Safex to keep client funds in the institutions' trust accounts rather than setting up their own trust accounts.
She said the requirement to keep client funds separately was introduced in the Stock Exchanges Control Act last year "as a significant enhancement to investor protection".
"It provides that members must keep a trust account in which they deposit funds due to a client or that had been received from a client before they are used," Newton-King said.
"In practice we have found that members prefer to keep the funds in an account maintained by the JSE Trustees (Pty) Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of the JSE which is a trust account."
The amendment in the Stock Exchanges Control Amendment Bill could make this legal and would reduce the administrative load on brokers.
The Financial Markets Control Amendment Bill also contains an amendment to allow members of Safex, for example, to deposit client funds into the JSE or Safex trust accounts.
The two bills, which mainly contained technical changes, will now be forwarded to parliament for approval.
Newton-King said that securities legislation generally would be amalgamated into one omnibus Act next year for easier reference and amendment.
